sections.h2: What is different about selling a house in Miami Gardens?
sections.html:
Miami Gardens requires a Certificate of Re-Occupancy before a property is purchased, sold, conveyed or transferred. That city step comes before closing, so build it into your timeline from day one.

The city's code compliance guide for property owners says the certificate takes five to seven business days when all information is provided. It exists to help the city track changes to structures, and it applies whether you list with an agent or take a cash offer.

  • Request the certificate early, before a contract date forces a rush.
  • Bring permits for any work done on the house.
  • Ask the city whether open violations or liens are recorded against the parcel.

sections.h2: How does the Miami Gardens re-occupancy certificate work?
sections.html:
The owner applies through the city's code enforcement and business licensing office, which can be reached at reoccupancy@miamigardens-fl.gov. The city inspects for changes made without a permit, and altered space such as added square footage is reported to the county so the property record and taxes can be corrected.

Violations do not stop a sale. The guide says a sale can go ahead as long as the buyer signs a stipulation agreement with the city promising to fix the problems. That matters for cash sales of worn houses, because a buyer who agrees to cure the violations can still close.

Unpermitted work is handled by legalizing it, which means securing a permit after the fact. The guide warns that this can bring penalties, and in the worst case demolition of the structure, so find out before you list.

Table 1. Miami Gardens steps before a sale, from the city's property owner guide
ItemWhat the city guide says
Certificate of Re-OccupancyRequired before purchase, sale, conveyance or transfer of title; 5 to 7 business days when information is complete
Unpermitted workMust be legalized by securing a permit
Open violationsSale can proceed if the buyer signs a stipulation agreement with the city
Landlord PermitRenewable each year on or before March 31
LiensCity lists lien searches, administrative release and lien amnesty or reduction

sections.h2: What work in Miami Gardens needs a permit?
sections.html:
The city lists fences, hurricane shutters, door and window installations, sheds, screen enclosures, pool barriers, patio slabs, gazebos, plumbing and electrical work, air conditioner change-outs, room additions and sea walls. The list is not complete, so call the building department before assuming anything is exempt.

A seller who replaced an air conditioner, closed in a patio or added a shed should look for the permit paperwork now. Missing permits are the usual reason a re-occupancy inspection takes longer than expected.

Other yard and street rules in the guide can also draw citations before a sale: open-air storage is prohibited, portable storage containers should be removed within thirty calendar days, and vehicles on the swale or public right of way may be towed. Clear those items before an inspector or buyer visits.

sections.h2: Do landlord rules affect a Miami Gardens house sale?
sections.html:
If the house is a rental, the owner needs a Landlord Permit, renewable each year on or before March 31. The application needs the permit fee, the names and birthdates of all occupants, and a national background check for occupants aged 15 and over.

A tenant in place changes the sale. Under Florida law the notice for unpaid rent is 3 days, excluding weekends and court holidays, and a month-to-month tenancy needs at least 30 days' notice to end. After a landlord wins in court, the sheriff puts the landlord in possession after 24 hours' posted notice.

A buyer paying cash for a rented house may want it vacant, may keep the tenant, or may ask you to deliver it empty. Put that choice in the contract so nobody guesses at closing.

sections.h2: What does Miami-Dade charge on a Miami Gardens deed?
sections.html:
Miami Gardens sits in Miami-Dade County, so the county's deed stamp rate applies. The Department of Revenue prints 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, and the surtax is not due on a document that transfers only a single-family dwelling.

The clerk collects the tax at recording, and all parties to the deed are liable for it. Taxable documents include warranty, special warranty, quit claim and trustee's deeds, and a deed in lieu of foreclosure. Clerk recording fees under section 28.24 start at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus trust fund and technology charges.

sections.h2: How do property taxes and exemptions work in Miami Gardens?
sections.html:
The Miami-Dade property appraiser values the parcel, and the county tax collector sends the bill. The appraiser's office says it does not send tax bills or set taxes, and it certified the 2026 roll on October 16, 2026.

Florida's calendar runs from a January 1 valuation date to a March 1 exemption deadline, with proposed notices in August and bills in November. Unpaid bills become delinquent on April 1, and tax certificates are sold by June 1.

A sale resets the assessed value to just value the following January 1 for the buyer, and the seller's homestead exemption ends. Sellers moving to another Florida home can ask about portability, which must be filed with the homestead application by March 1.

  • Ask the title company to prorate this year's tax at closing.
  • Confirm that no tax certificate has been sold on the parcel.
  • Ask the appraiser about any changes reported after a city inspection.

sections.h2: What if the Miami Gardens house is in foreclosure or probate?
sections.html:
Foreclosure moves on a court timeline. After final judgment the clerk's sale is set not less than 20 and not more than 35 days out, unless the plaintiff agrees to a longer period, and homeowners are told to check with the clerk within 10 days after a sale about surplus funds.

For an inherited house, Florida's summary administration covers estates of $150,000 or less in non-exempt property, or deaths more than two years ago. Creditor claims are barred after the later of three months from first publication of the notice or 30 days after service on a creditor who had to be served.

In either case, ask a Florida attorney or the clerk's self-help staff what documents a title company will want before it insures the sale.

sections.h2: How do I judge a cash offer in Miami Gardens?
sections.html:
Compare the net cash after every cost, then read who handles the re-occupancy certificate, any city lien payoff and the deed stamp tax. A buyer who takes the house as is should still say in writing who pays for city fees and who signs a stipulation agreement.

Ask for the closing date, the title company's name and the deposit terms before you sign.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate to sell a house in Miami Gardens?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's property owner guide says a Certificate of Re-Occupancy is required before the purchase, sale, conveyance or transfer of title of any real property, with a turnaround of five to seven business days when information is complete.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Miami Gardens house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes, if the buyer enters a stipulation agreement with the city promising to fix the violations, according to the city's guide. Unpermitted work has to be legalized through a permit.

faqs.q: When is the Miami Gardens landlord permit due?
faqs.a: It renews each year on or before March 31. The application needs the fee, all occupants' names and birthdates and a national background check for occupants aged 15 and over.

faqs.q: What deed stamp tax applies in Miami Gardens?
faqs.a: Miami-Dade County uses 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax that is not due on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling, as printed by the Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill for a Miami Gardens home?
faqs.a: The Miami-Dade County tax collector. The property appraiser values the property and states that it does not send bills or collect taxes.
